scenario.description: A software development team is tasked with implementing a new user authentication module. The Project Lead, acting as the Orchestrator (A1), receives the core requirements and a critical security constraint. The Lead then delegates the task to two parallel sub-teams: the Frontend Lead (A2) and the Backend Lead (A3). The Frontend Lead (A2) is responsible for the user interface and passes their design to a UI/UX Developer (A4) for implementation details. Concurrently, the Backend Lead (A3) focuses on API development and passes their architectural plan to a Database Engineer (A5) for schema design and integration. Both the UI/UX Developer and the Database Engineer must ensure the critical security constraint is upheld in their respective outputs. The core constraint dictates that 'all user passwords must be hashed using Argon2id with a minimum memory cost of 2^20 KiB and a time cost of 4 iterations.' This setup evaluates whether this precise technical security constraint propagates accurately down both branches of the development team, from high-level design to low-level implementation, without being diluted or lost.
